stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: An NPN transistor has three operating regions set by the base current $I_B$. Sweep $I_B$ from $0$ to $160\,\mu\text{A}$ and watch the operating point crawl along the load line. Reach the cut-off region ($I_B \approx 0$), the active region (middle), and saturation ($I_B > I_{B,sat}$) to advance.
stages.concept: Cut-off ($I_B = 0$): $I_C \approx 0$, $V_{CE} \approx V_{CC}$. Active: $I_C = \beta I_B$, so $V_{CE} = V_{CC} - \beta I_B R_C$. Saturation ($I_B \geq I_{B,sat}$): $V_{CE}$ clamps at $V_{CE,sat} \approx 0.2\,\text{V}$, so $I_C \approx V_{CC}/R_C$ — pushing $I_B$ higher changes nothing.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: The transistor can operate as a switch or as an amplifier. In SWITCH mode a square wave $I_B(t)$ toggles the transistor between cut-off and saturation — the collector lamp blinks. In AMPLIFIER mode a small sinusoid $i_b(t)$ around a mid-active bias produces an inverted, amplified $V_{CE}(t)$. Toggle both modes to advance.
stages.concept: Switch mode drives $V_{CE}$ between $V_{CC}$ and $V_{CE,sat}$ — the output is a rail-to-rail square wave. Amplifier mode holds the bias in the active region so small $\Delta I_B$ maps linearly to $\Delta V_{CE} = -\beta R_C \Delta I_B$: gain $= -\beta R_C / r$ (inverted).

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The scope shows a target $V_{CE}(t)$ produced by a hidden $I_B(t)$. Compute on paper first: which operating regime does this waveform belong to — cut-off, active, or saturated? Pick the mode, then SUBMIT. Miss any scenario and the deck restarts from the top.
stages.concept: A flat $V_{CE} \approx V_{CC}$ trace means the transistor never conducts — cut-off. A clean inverted sinusoid means the bias sits inside the active region and stays there — active. A square-ish clipped trace slamming between the two rails means $I_B$ swings past $I_{B,sat}$ and pins $V_{CE}$ at $V_{CE,sat}$ on the peaks — saturated.

labels.tip1: sweep I_B · reach cut-off, active, and saturation
labels.tip2: toggle SWITCH and AMPLIFIER · watch V_CE change shape
labels.tip3: read the target · name the regime · SUBMIT
labels.peek_tip_1: Flat V_CE = V_CC means no conduction. Clipped square = both rails reached. Clean sine inside the rails = active linear region.
labels.peek_tip_2: In saturation I_C is capped at V_CC/R_C — beta stops mattering. In active I_C = beta*I_B so V_CE tracks I_B linearly.

1.1: Start at I_B = 0. The lamp is off, V_CE sits at V_CC — that's cut-off.
1.2: Push I_B up to about 60 uA. V_CE drops to roughly the middle — that's the active region.
1.3: Beyond I_B = 120 uA (I_B,sat), V_CE flatlines at V_CE,sat ~ 0.2V — that's saturation. Visit all three.

2.1: SWITCH mode: input is a square wave, output slams between V_CC and V_CE,sat — the lamp blinks.
2.2: AMPLIFIER mode: input is a small sinusoid biased mid-active. V_CE is a scaled, INVERTED sinusoid.
2.3: Click both mode buttons to toggle between them at least once.

3.1: First: is the target waveform flat, sinusoidal, or clipped square? That decides the regime.
3.2: Compute I_B,sat = V_CC / (beta * R_C) = 12 / (100 * 1000) = 120 uA. If I_B stays below, it's active.
3.3: Flat at V_CC -> cut-off. Sine that never touches the rails -> active. Square clipped at both rails -> saturated.
